subject: Novamed DPA redlines & SCCs - role split, transfer addendum and escalation path
messages:
From: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@novamed.eu>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novamed Legal <legal@novamed.eu>
Date: Mon, 15 Dec 2025 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: DPA redline set + SCCs / role split question

Hi Marissa / Ben,

Thanks for the call yesterday. Attached is our third pass on the DPA with in-line comments (Novamed_DPA_Redlines_v3.docx). Two items that are blocking internal sign-off on our side:

- Controller/Processor role split in Section 2. We still need an explicit statement that Novamed will remain controller for patient identifiers and Redwood will be processor for hosted inference logs. Your previous language made this implicit; our counsel wants explicit delineation.
- SCCs: comment on Appendix A regarding subprocessors — Novamed wants a 30 day notice period for new subprocessors for EU-hosted data (we currently have 10).
- Transfer addendum: we propose a short transfer impact addendum to sit behind the MSA that clarifies export paths and fallback to EU-only hosting if transfers are restricted.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept the wording on the role split and extend the subprocessor notice to 30 days? If not, we need to escalate to legal to see if a compensating control (KMS/HSM audit schedule + SOC2 attestation line) will be acceptable instead.

Also looping Thomas Berger from product for any technical clarifications on hosting regions.

Attachments: Novamed_DPA_Redlines_v3.docx (redlines)

Best,
Anna Müller
Head of Legal Ops
Novamed GmbH

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@novamed.eu>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Thomas Berger <t.berger@novamed.eu>
Date: Mon, 15 Dec 2025 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA redline set + SCCs / role split question

Hi Anna — thanks for the packet and clear notes. We pulled legal and product into the thread to speed this up. Quick answers below and an internal ask.

- Role split: Redwood's preferred language is to stay as a processor for processing related to customers' data and to reserve controller status only where we collect account-level billing information or as required by law. We can accept an explicit sentence that mirrors that split (we'll send a proposed clause) but we cannot accept language that would reclassify inference outputs as solely customer-owned controller data without further review.

- Subprocessor notice window: 30 days is doable for EU-only hosting and for any subprocessors handling EU personal data; we can commit to 30 days notice for that scope. For global non-EU infra we need the current 10-day standard but we can scope that in the proposed clause.

- Transfer addendum: Product wants the fallback flow captured (EU-only hosting + escalation to dedicated / private deployment if transfers are restricted). That will affect pricing (order form). Ben — can you flag the pricing delta and attach a rough order-form markup?

Internal next steps:
1) Legal (Laura) to review Anna's redline and our annotated language.
2) Ben to produce a 1st-pass order form delta (OrderForm_V2_markup.xlsx).
3) Karthik / Product to confirm technical feasibility of the EU-only fallback and estimated lead time.

I've attached our annotated DPA (RI_DPA_annotated.pdf) with suggested language and a short summary. Can we target end-of-day Thursday (18 Dec) for a consolidated position from Redwood? If Novamed needs faster, please indicate priority and which clauses are must-have.

Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
Attachments: RI_DPA_annotated.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Anna Müller <anna.mueller@novamed.eu>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Dec 2025 13:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA redline set + SCCs / role split question

Thanks — short note from procurement/pricing side:

- EU-only fallback will be treated as an "opt-in" hosting addendum on the order form. Ballpark uplift for dedicated EU capacity is ~18-25% on top of hosted API unit pricing (depends on committed throughput).
- If Novamed needs guaranteed EU-only fallback (contractual SLA and delivery timelines), we need an implementation lead time of 8-10 weeks + acceptance testing window — call this out in the order form.
- I'll attach OrderForm_V2_markup.xlsx with two scenarios: (A) EU-fallback as optional paid add-on, (B) EU-fallback as included for a higher committed rate.

Action requested from Novamed: confirm which scenario you prefer and whether you want the 30-day subprocessor notice to apply only to scenario (A/B) where EU-only hosting is selected.

Ben Carter
Director, Solutions & Procurement
Redwood Inference
Attachment: OrderForm_V2_markup.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@novamed.eu>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Dec 2025 16:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: DPA redline set + SCCs / role split question

Anna — thanks for the clear redlines. I've reviewed Novamed_DPA_Redlines_v3.docx and Marissa's annotated draft. Below is Redwood legal's consolidated position (we'll follow up with an updated doc for signature-ready language).

1) Controller/Processor language: we will accept an explicit clause that states: "For the avoidance of doubt, to the extent Customer provides Personal Data to Redwood for inference or related services, Customer acts as Controller and Redwood acts as Processor, except where Redwood collects data for account administration or as required by law, in which case Redwood may process Customer data as Controller to the limited extent necessary." We will not accept language that treats model outputs as Customer-exclusive Controller content without a limited carveout for telemetry and operational debugging limited to [x] days retention — draft will include precise retention and auditability statements.

2) Subprocessor notice period: Redwood accepts a 30-day notice period for subprocessors that will process EU personal data when Novamed has selected EU-only hosting in the order form. For global hosting we will keep the existing 10-day notice. We'll provide the scoped language (see attached draft).

3) Transfer impact addendum: Redwood can provide a transfer-addendum that enumerates fallback flows and the operational steps to switch to EU-only hosting. However, explicit SLAs tied to a legal 'guarantee' of transfer availability will require procurement sign-off on pricing (Ben has the right path). Operational lead time is 8 weeks for dedicated provisioning; we'll include the testing and cutover plan in the addendum.

4) Next steps & timeline:
- Redwood will send a consolidated DPA + scoped SCCs redline by EOD Wednesday (17 Dec) for Novamed legal review.
- If Novamed confirms scenario (A/B) preference by Thursday EOD (18 Dec), Redwood will include the order form markup in the same package and surface the pricing delta.

DocuSign for the MSA + DPA will be prepared after signoff; Laura will lead legal handoff. HubSpot: record DEAL-8472 is updated with the latest redline package: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/8472

If Novamed wants to escalate to exec-level approval on mandatory SLA commitments, please advise and we can schedule a short call with our Head of Business (Marissa will coordinate).

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_DPA_consolidated_redline_v1.docx; DocuSign_prelim_link: https://docusign.com/ABC-123-novamed-dpa
